PR title: `R1 249: Round commands decide in the domain; Pulse commands and the Rounds view are scoped to the Team`
PR body (use exactly):

## Why
`runRoundCommand` decided every rejection inline inside its SQL transaction, so those rules could only be tested through workerd. Review on #250 also found an authorization gap: SkipWeek, UnskipWeek, PausePulse and ResumePulse authorized the command's Team but acted on any Pulse id. A Lead of one Team could pause another Team's Pulse in the same Organization and cancel its scheduled Round. Fixes #249.

## What changed
- New pure `decideRoundCommand` (`packages/domain/src/rounds/RoundCommand.ts`) returns Rejected, Unchanged or a plan per command, keeping the old check order. The adapter loads the Round, Invitation and pending-compute flag, calls it, and applies the plan with the same writes in the same order.
- Security: the four Pulse commands refuse `PulseNotFound` unless the Pulse belongs to the authorized Team (team-scoped `findPulse`, now exported). The reviewer found the same gap in `viewRounds` (`GET /teams/:teamId/pulses/:pulseId/rounds` returned another Team's Rounds); it gets the same check.

## Verification
- 73 domain tests, including a property that a Lead of one Team is refused all four Pulse commands on another Team's Pulse while that Team's Lead still succeeds. Planted bugs (unscoped lookup, Forbidden before RoundNotFound, eight-week range off by one, effectiveN ignoring the directory minimum) each fail tests.
- Adapter: the Round lifecycle route creates a second Team whose Lead is refused both `viewRounds` and `PausePulse` on the first Team's Pulse. It fails with the `viewRounds` check removed.
- Fence gate: typecheck, lint, format, ledgers, 1283 unit, 241 privacy tests.

Return the PR URL and head SHA.
